html:
The Congress of Berlin was a meeting of the great powers of Europe in June and July 1878 that redrew the map of the Balkans after the Russo-Turkish War of 1877 to 1878.

Russia had won the war and imposed the Treaty of San Stefano on the Ottoman Empire, creating a large Bulgaria under Russian influence. Britain and Austria-Hungary would not accept it. The German chancellor Otto von Bismarck, calling himself an "honest broker", hosted the powers in Berlin to settle the matter.

The results:

  • Serbia, Montenegro and Romania became fully independent.
  • Bulgaria was cut to a smaller self-governing principality; the south became the Ottoman province of Eastern Rumelia, and Macedonia went back to Ottoman rule.
  • Austria-Hungary was allowed to occupy and run Bosnia and Herzegovina.
  • Russia gained southern Bessarabia and Kars and Batumi in the Caucasus.
  • Britain took over Cyprus by a separate deal with the Ottomans.

The settlement kept the peace among the powers for a time, but it left Russians, Bulgarians and Serbs angry. Their grievances fed the Bosnian crisis of 1908, the Balkan Wars and, in the end, the First World War.
sum: The Congress of Berlin was a meeting of the great powers of Europe in June and July 1878 that redrew the map of the Balkans after the Russo-Turkish War of 1877 to 1878.
